text:
maria: heads-up: ops alerted that prefix/KV cache hit-rate tanked after the attention-kernel swap deployed at 02:10 UTC. baseline traffic shows a big delta in warmup behav.
cheng: details? which deploy exactly (commit/flag)?
ops-bot: alert: cache_hit_rate.service_prefix_cache P90 drop 95.8% -> 61.3% (window: 02:12–02:40 UTC). spike in token-generation cost. incident id INC-2026-324
devon: saw the same in prod metrics. P50 gen latency moved 42ms -> 78ms and token-cost up ~1.9x on the affected model family. No obvious increase in request rate.
anita: we also rolled quantization profile updates in the same deploy (int8 path for attn fusion). could be interplay.
leo: quick repro: call hosted endpoint with the same prompt twice in sequence. second call should hit prefix cache. with new kernel second call misses ~70% of the time.
maria: repro steps please (curl or SDK) so SRE can verify.
leo: repro snippet:
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-7b-fused","input":"Summarize: The quick brown fox...","session_id":"repro-123"}'
# repeat same call within 500ms -> expect cache hit
```
cheng: can you attach the kernel variant flag used? I suspect the attention kernel changed how KV keys are serialized (float16 rounding differences or ordering of small attrs), which would bork key normalization.
leo: flag was `--attn-kern=flash-v2` and we enabled `--kv-compact=true` in the same docker image (image: rwd-runtime:2026-03-08-5f2c)
devon: grabbed a few sample cache keys from logs. old keys:
```
pk:sha256:3b7a...:len=192:tok0=118
pk:sha256:3b7a...:len=192:tok0=118
```
new keys look similar but hashes are different for identical prompts:
```
pk:sha256:8f9e...:len=192:tok0=118
```
Which implies canonicalization variation.
anita: also checked kv cache profiling: warmup traffic pre-deploy had ~96% reuse for common prompt templates. post-deploy templates show ~40-65% reuse depending on tokenization boundary. maybe tokenization changes? did BPE pipeline update?
cheng: tokenizer wasn't touched in this deploy. my hunch: kernel now writes KV meta in a slightly different layout (padding order) which our key-hash pipeline consumes before normalization. Need to inspect both serializer and the kernel output shape/dtype.
maria: urgent ask: is this causing user-facing errors or just cost/latency regression?
devon: mostly cost/latency. A few customers noticed degraded perf on chat flows with long prefixes; no data leaks. SLA impacts low but cost spike measurable.
leo: quick experiment: set `RUNTIME_FLAG_PREFIX_KEY_NORMALIZE=1` in a canary host, which forces explicit normalization path (old code). canary shows hit-rate back to ~94% for the sampled prompts.
cheng: good. that suggests fallback normalization fixes keys. short-term mitigation: flip the flag cluster-wide for affected model pool. long-term: add a deterministic canonicalization step in the serializer and add unit tests for kernel compatibility.
maria: action items?
cheng: 1) roll flag to all nodes in the pool (ops) 2) open a runtime bug: kernel-output-keying mismatch (assign to eng-runtime) 3) add integration test: recompile kernel variants and validate key parity on a canonical prompt set 4) follow up on whether quant profile contributed (assign to anita)
maria: devon/ops -- can you coordinate the flag rollout and monitor cost delta? start with 5% traffic -> 25% -> full.
devon: starting 5% now. will post metrics in this thread. rolling back kernel would be last resort.
ops-bot: deploy job started: rollout-rw-prefix-fix -> 5% at 03:05 UTC
leo: I'll instrument a quick parity-check tool that computes key hash from kernel output vs current serializer and logs diffs.
anita: I'll re-run quantization unit tests with `flash-v2` to check numeric drift leading to different key bytes.
cheng: add a regression test into CI that runs `flash-v2`+kv-compact on the short canonical prompt list and asserts identical key hash with the reference kernel.
maria: timeline?
leo: parity tool by EOD. dev rollout metrics should show improvement in ~15-20m after canary.
devon: canary 5% shows hit-rate climbing to 88% on that cohort within 10m. cost trending down.
ops-bot: deploy job progressed: 25% at 03:25 UTC
devon: at 25% rollout, cluster-wide hit-rate ~90% and P50 latency back to ~46ms on affected model family. keeping rollout.
cheng: creating ENG-RT-1274 with logs and suggested fixes.
maria: thanks everyone. let's keep thread pinned to incident and post final RCA after kernel fix goes out.
cheng: RCA will include: root cause = kernel changed KV meta layout/serialization leading to non-deterministic key bytes; contributing factors = simultaneous `kv-compact` flag + quant profile change. Fix = normalize keys in serializer + add CI parity tests + backported stable kernel variant; short-term = enable PREFIX_KEY_NORMALIZE flag.
leo: leaving a final note: add a lightweight end-to-end check in the deploy pipeline that exercises prefix caching behavior for one sample prompt before promoting kernel variants.
maria: ack. good catch. :thumbsup:
